Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: "Nothing gold can stay": decoupling factor decay from state persistence
ideas.description: Pulse-stimulate cells, wash out, and run matched time courses of FOS/JUN protein levels (quantitative immunoblot, Halo-tag pulse-chase) against chromatin accessibility and nucleosome positioning at AP-1 motifs (ATAC-seq plus AP-1 CUT&RUN). Memory is supported only if the accessible state at AP-1-bound enhancers outlives the protein by many half-lives; co-decay would instead indicate ongoing signaling rather than memory.

ideas.title: "So dawn goes down to day": testing the handoff to a durable successor
ideas.description: Perform time-resolved CUT&RUN for FOS, FOSB, FRA1/FRA2, JUN, JUNB, and JUND together with co-IP of dimer composition at matched timepoints, asking whether labile FOS-containing dimers at a given site are replaced by longer-lived FRA1/JUND dimers or by resident lineage factors. A site-preserving compositional handoff is the concrete mechanistic form that AP-1 memory would need to take.

ideas.title: "Her hardest hue to hold": mitotic dilution as the decay clock
ideas.description: Pair a stimulus pulse with FUCCI/live imaging and with cell-cycle arrest (CDK4/6 inhibition or contact arrest), then measure how many divisions the primed state survives using re-stimulation reporters and ATAC-seq on cells sorted by division number via dye dilution. Decay scaling with divisions implies a replication-coupled chromatin carrier, whereas decay on wall-clock time regardless of division implicates slow protein or RNA turnover.

ideas.title: "But only so an hour": degron separation of establishment versus maintenance
ideas.description: Tag endogenous FOS and JUN with dTAG or AID degrons and deplete them either before stimulation, during the first hour of response, or only after the state is established. A memory function requires that post-establishment depletion preserves primed accessibility and accelerated secondary responses, while early depletion abolishes both.

ideas.title: "Then leaf subsides to leaf": clone-resolved second-hit restimulation
ideas.description: Lineage-barcode cells, stimulate, allow a long rest period, then restimulate and use single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq to ask whether enhanced re-induction is heritable within clones rather than merely a population average. Shared priming among sister cells of the same clone distinguishes a genuinely inherited chromatin state from averaging over transient responders.
